# OPENING: Christ had no biological father

**Position [L4].** The KJV says Jesus was conceived in Mary by the Holy Ghost, with no man involved. Joseph was his legal and supposed father, not his begetter. By "biological father" I mean a male who begets the child by natural generation. I make no claim about anything beyond the text.

## 1. The conception is "of the Holy Ghost," and no man is named

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- **[L2]** The phrase is *ek pneumatos hagiou* (G1537, G4151, G40), "out of the Spirit, holy." The preposition *ek* marks source or origin. The verse names the origin of the pregnancy, and the origin is not a man.
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
- **[L2]** The verb is *gennēthen* (G1080, *gennaō*), "begotten or conceived." The same word is used of fathers begetting in Matthew 1:2–16. In Matthew 1:20 it is applied to what is "in her," with the Holy Ghost as source.
- **[L3]** John 4:24: "God is a Spirit." The source named in Matthew 1:20 is therefore not a male body, so the begetting is not biological in the ordinary sense.
- **[L4]** Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 name the source of the conception as the Holy Ghost. John 4:24 says that source is spirit, not flesh. Together they show the conception did not come from a male human parent.

## 2. Matthew's genealogy breaks its own pattern at verse 16

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
- **[L2]** Verses 2–15 repeat *egennēsen* (G1080), "begat," with a male subject. Verse 16 changes to *egennēthē*, "was born," a passive form. The relative pronoun *hēs* (G3739) is feminine singular, "of whom [her]." The birth is traced to Mary alone, and Joseph is called only "the husband of Mary."
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob." This is the pattern the genealogy sets, and verse 16 departs from it at the last link.
- **[L4]** The chain of "begat" ends at Joseph. Jesus is not said to be begotten by him. He is "born" of Mary, who is named as the sole parent.

## 3. Mary was a virgin and says so

- **[L1]** Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph… and the virgin's name was Mary."
- **[L2]** *Parthenos* (G3933), "virgin."
- **[L1]** Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
- **[L2]** *ginōskō* (G1097), "to know," used here of sexual knowledge, with *anēr* (G435), "a man, a male."
- **[L1]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
- **[L2]** *dio kai*, "wherefore also," makes the cause explicit. The child is called Son of God because of the Holy Ghost's coming. A male parent is not named.
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." Joseph's *ginōskō* is withheld until the birth.
- **[L4]** Mary's question in Luke 1:34 is answered by the Holy Ghost's coming in 1:35, with no mention of any man. Matthew 1:25 confirms Joseph had no part before the birth.

## 4. The prophecies point the same way

- **[L1]** Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."
- **[L2]** *almah* (H5959) is the Hebrew word the KJV renders "virgin." *Harah* (H2029), "conceive," is the verb of the sign, and the sign is the conception itself.
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:23: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son… Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us."
- **[L3]** Genesis 3:15: "between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head." The promised deliverer is called "her seed" (*zera*, H2233, "seed"), the woman's seed and not the man's.
- **[L3]** Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman." The verb *genomenon* (G1096) means "made, become," and the source named is *ek gynaikos* (G1135, "out of a woman"), not a man.
- **[L4]** Genesis 3:15 names the woman's seed, Isaiah 7:14 gives a virgin conceiving, and Galatians 4:4 names only "a woman." Together these form one line of text that names no human male source.

## 5. Joseph is the supposed father only

- **[L1]** Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."
- **[L2]** *enomizeto* (G3543, *nomizō*), "was thought, was reckoned." It marks opinion or legal reckoning as opposed to fact.
- **[L1]** Luke 2:48: "Thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." Mary speaks of Joseph as "father."
- **[L3]** Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" The child corrects the title and points to a different Father.
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:19–20: Joseph is told to "take unto thee Mary thy wife." Taking and naming (Matthew 1:21, 25) are acts of adoption and legal fatherhood.
- **[L4]** Luke 3:23 marks Joseph's fatherhood as supposed. Luke 2:49 names another Father. Matthew 1:20, 25 describe Joseph's role as taking and naming, not begetting. Joseph is legal father only.

## 6. The royal line gives a further reason

- **[L2]** *zera* (H2233), "seed," is the word here for physical descendants.

- [L1] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph, which was [the son] of Heli," and [L3] Luke 3:24: "Which was [the son] of Matthat, which was [the son] of Levi." Luke also carries the line man by man through Joseph.
- [L2] nomizō (G3543), "properly, to do by law (usage)... suppose, be wont." [L3] Acts 16:13 uses the same form of custom: "where prayer was wont to be made." Luke 2:44 uses the word of a supposition: "supposing him to have been in the company." So the word does not decide the matter by itself. - Matthew 1:12, "Jechonias begat Salathiel," and Luke 3:27, "which was [the son] of Salathiel, which was [the son] of Neri," are held as written and are not joined.

## C5: The order is: the espousal, the finding, the taking, then abstinence until the birth. KEPT.

- [L1] Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." This verse dates the finding.

- [L3] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" [L2] ginōskō (G1097), "to know," stands there in the present tense. It gives her state when the angel spoke, not a vow.

## C6: The flesh is David's seed. KEPT.

- [L1] Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh;" [L3] Romans 1:4: "And declared [to be] the Son of God with power, according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead: [declared: Gr. determined]." ## The record's reading, in sum

The promise is "thy seed... which shall proceed out of thy bowels" (2 Samuel 7:12) and "the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh" (Acts 2:30). It is fulfilled in one "made of the seed of David according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3).

The text names the man. He is "Joseph, thou son of David" (Matthew 1:20), "Joseph her husband" (Matthew 1:19), and "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph" in a disciple's mouth (John 1:45). He is "thy father" in his mother's own words (Luke 2:48).

His tribe was "evident" (Hebrews 7:14) by the law's measure, "by the house of their fathers" (Numbers 1:18).

"That which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" is the angel's ground for "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife" (Matthew 1:20). It names the seed God claims as his son: "I will be his father, and he shall be my son" (2 Samuel 7:14).

Christ had a biological father: Joseph, the named son of David, of whose loins the promised seed came.

RULE E-ANS (an answer to a pressed verse). Decide FIRST what the right grade is: MEETS only when the answer shows, in its own words, how the verse fits the answering side's case, or why the stated meaning does not follow from what the verse says. MISSES when the answer rests on an absence (it says only that the verse, or the other side, names no, states no, does not name, gives no, or is silent on something) without a fit of its own, or when it does not address the stated meaning. An answer that quotes the verse's own words against the specific claim of the stated meaning (for example, the verse's own stated grounds set against a claim that there were no grounds) shows why the meaning does not follow: it MEETS, even when it closes with a bare assertion such as "It fits the link". Then for each judge's grade: AGREE when it matches the right grade, DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-VOID (a listed premise ruled VOID). A premise is VOID only when its charge says the opponent's quoted words state something they do not state (a negation, a universal, or another claim beyond the quote). The charge is the premise's own words before its quote (for example "The inference that ..."), read against the words of that quote. Set aside only a clause saying what the premise props ("which props ...") or a sentence naming the objection it serves ("The objection it props is ..."); those are not part of the charge. AGREE with the VOID ruling when the charge goes beyond its quote; DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-COL (a collision line: FORCED, or LINK BROKEN). A link is broken only when the answer's own quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, as the line quotes them; it is not broken because no verse states it, or because of an absence, and it is not broken by a rival reading: an answer that reads a contested word another way, with its own layers quoted in its round, can agree with the meaning on its own reading (pkgECF, W3 2534; either side alike). A link is also broken when a proven press against it was left unanswered (Commitment 5) and the line quotes the pressing sentence and names its round (ruling 392); that is not a break by absence. When the item says the FAILS words are found exactly in the round of the answer, those words are the answering side's own and are read as part of its answer. AGREE when the quoted words show the answer cannot agree with the meaning; DISAGREE when they do carry a meaning the link can agree with, or the line rests on an absence or on a demand for a stating verse. A line's layers after GROUND ([L1], [L2], [L3]; Commitment 13) are counted in code, not by you: read them as the judge's grounds.
RULE E-SYN (a sentence of the synthesis saying a side withdrew, conceded, granted, dropped or narrowed something). AGREE when that side's own sentences given you give up that same thing at the same scope; DISAGREE when they do not, or give up less (for example, "no row I cite" is not "no biblical text").
RULE E-HOLD (a collision line graded STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED). STANDS is right only when the answering side's own words, as quoted to you in the line or in this judge's ANSWER CHECK lines, carry a meaning the link can agree with for the meaning pressed. UNDERDETERMINED is right only when the quoted words show that both readings agree with the pressed verse and neither side's words show that the other cannot. BROKEN when the answer's quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, or the answer is only a bare grant or an absence with no fit of its own. A ground that rests on an absence (no verse states it, the text does not narrate it), or on the judge's own reading rather than the debate's words, is not a ground. Each ANSWER CHECK line given you is labelled with whose answer it grades: a MISSES or FAILS on the challenger's answer counts against the challenger's link, never against the defender's, and the reverse. A press labelled UNPROVEN carries no answering burden, so a MISSES on it breaks nothing. For a link-state line ("D5: STANDS"), the quoted answers are that side's ANSWER CHECK lines given you: STANDS is right unless one of them, on a press against this link, is MISSES or FAILS. AGREE when the judge's grade is right; DISAGREE when it is not.
RULE E-KEY (the keystone line). The keystone grade must follow from this judge's own collision lines on that link, given to you: STANDS only when none of them grades the link BROKEN or FORCED and the link was not withdrawn; BROKEN when one of them does. Its ground, where it gives one, must rest on the debate's words, not on the judge's own statement of doctrine. AGREE when the keystone grade follows and its ground rests on the debate's words; DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-PREM (a listed premise, and how each judge ruled it). The judges' own rules, quoted: "A LINK ROUND answer that neither exhibits the premise's layer footing nor concedes counts as CONCEDED." "SELF-SUPPORTED = every listed defender claim is carried by its layer stack -- each [L4] exhibits the [L1]/[L2]/[L3] footing it rests on (at least two prior layers exhibited; a shown chain counts equally)." For a charge in the form ASSUMES: ... -- ROWS GIVE: ...: "the premise is UNEXHIBITED when no quoted row gives the fact it assumes, and it stands when a row the side quoted gives that fact." "UNEXHIBITED also fires ... when a narrowed link keeps words that still assert what its own side gave up." And: "What a link INFERS from its rows is its [L4]: it is graded by the two-layer rule and by the meaning of the verses pressed against it, and never as a missing row (DG-61); an inferred act, such as a begetting or a knowing, is never an ASSUMES." A premise "charged in terms stronger than its quote, is VOID" (RULE E-VOID). For premise N only, decide FIRST the right ruling: COUNTED (UNEXHIBITED or CONCEDED), SPARED, or VOID. The judges' form reads "Itemize the counted links": a premise the judge's line does not name is that judge's SPARED ruling. AGREE when the judge's ruling on premise N (named, or spared by silence) is the right one; DISAGREE when it is not; NO ANSWER only when the judge's line is not in its form. A NARROWED premise (the side drops a claim and keeps the link on a narrower footing, with its [L1] and [L2] or [L3] exhibited) is SPARED: dropping a claim is not conceding the premise, and the dropped claim alone never makes the premise COUNTED. It is UNEXHIBITED only when the kept words still assert the very claim the side dropped; say so by quoting both the dropped claim and the kept words that still assert it.
RULE E-RES (a judge's RESULT line). Its arithmetic is checked in code. Read only its reason sentence: by the judges' Commitment 1 (the record is the only evidence) and Commitment 3 (ruling 405), a reason that rests on an absence (no verse states it, the text does not narrate it) or on the judge's own doctrine rather than the debate's words is not a reason. FOLLOWS when the reason rests on the debate's words; DOES NOT FOLLOW when it does not, quoting the words that show it. AGREE when FOLLOWS; DISAGREE when DOES NOT FOLLOW.
NO ANSWER, for every rule: the judge's line lacks its grade or its ground, or is not in its form. It reports a violation by the judge; it is never your own uncertainty, and you choose AGREE or DISAGREE whenever the line can be read.

RULE E-ANS (an answer to a pressed verse). Decide FIRST what the right grade is: MEETS only when the answer shows, in its own words, how the verse fits the answering side's case, or why the stated meaning does not follow from what the verse says. MISSES when the answer rests on an absence (it says only that the verse, or the other side, names no, states no, does not name, gives no, or is silent on something) without a fit of its own, or when it does not address the stated meaning. An answer that quotes the verse's own words against the specific claim of the stated meaning (for example, the verse's own stated grounds set against a claim that there were no grounds) shows why the meaning does not follow: it MEETS, even when it closes with a bare assertion such as "It fits the link". Then for each judge's grade: AGREE when it matches the right grade, DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-VOID (a listed premise ruled VOID). A premise is VOID only when its charge says the opponent's quoted words state something they do not state (a negation, a universal, or another claim beyond the quote). The charge is the premise's own words before its quote (for example "The inference that ..."), read against the words of that quote. Set aside only a clause saying what the premise props ("which props ...") or a sentence naming the objection it serves ("The objection it props is ..."); those are not part of the charge. AGREE with the VOID ruling when the charge goes beyond its quote; DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-COL (a collision line: FORCED, or LINK BROKEN). A link is broken only when the answer's own quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, as the line quotes them; it is not broken because no verse states it, or because of an absence, and it is not broken by a rival reading: an answer that reads a contested word another way, with its own layers quoted in its round, can agree with the meaning on its own reading (pkgECF, W3 2534; either side alike). A link is also broken when a proven press against it was left unanswered (Commitment 5) and the line quotes the pressing sentence and names its round (ruling 392); that is not a break by absence. When the item says the FAILS words are found exactly in the round of the answer, those words are the answering side's own and are read as part of its answer. AGREE when the quoted words show the answer cannot agree with the meaning; DISAGREE when they do carry a meaning the link can agree with, or the line rests on an absence or on a demand for a stating verse. A line's layers after GROUND ([L1], [L2], [L3]; Commitment 13) are counted in code, not by you: read them as the judge's grounds.
RULE E-SYN (a sentence of the synthesis saying a side withdrew, conceded, granted, dropped or narrowed something). AGREE when that side's own sentences given you give up that same thing at the same scope; DISAGREE when they do not, or give up less (for example, "no row I cite" is not "no biblical text").
RULE E-HOLD (a collision line graded STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED). STANDS is right only when the answering side's own words, as quoted to you in the line or in this judge's ANSWER CHECK lines, carry a meaning the link can agree with for the meaning pressed. UNDERDETERMINED is right only when the quoted words show that both readings agree with the pressed verse and neither side's words show that the other cannot. BROKEN when the answer's quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, or the answer is only a bare grant or an absence with no fit of its own. A ground that rests on an absence (no verse states it, the text does not narrate it), or on the judge's own reading rather than the debate's words, is not a ground. Each ANSWER CHECK line given you is labelled with whose answer it grades: a MISSES or FAILS on the challenger's answer counts against the challenger's link, never against the defender's, and the reverse. A press labelled UNPROVEN carries no answering burden, so a MISSES on it breaks nothing. For a link-state line ("D5: STANDS"), the quoted answers are that side's ANSWER CHECK lines given you: STANDS is right unless one of them, on a press against this link, is MISSES or FAILS. AGREE when the judge's grade is right; DISAGREE when it is not.
RULE E-KEY (the keystone line). The keystone grade must follow from this judge's own collision lines on that link, given to you: STANDS only when none of them grades the link BROKEN or FORCED and the link was not withdrawn; BROKEN when one of them does. Its ground, where it gives one, must rest on the debate's words, not on the judge's own statement of doctrine. AGREE when the keystone grade follows and its ground rests on the debate's words; DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-PREM (a listed premise, and how each judge ruled it). The judges' own rules, quoted: "A LINK ROUND answer that neither exhibits the premise's layer footing nor concedes counts as CONCEDED." "SELF-SUPPORTED = every listed defender claim is carried by its layer stack -- each [L4] exhibits the [L1]/[L2]/[L3] footing it rests on (at least two prior layers exhibited; a shown chain counts equally)." For a charge in the form ASSUMES: ... -- ROWS GIVE: ...: "the premise is UNEXHIBITED when no quoted row gives the fact it assumes, and it stands when a row the side quoted gives that fact." "UNEXHIBITED also fires ... when a narrowed link keeps words that still assert what its own side gave up." And: "What a link INFERS from its rows is its [L4]: it is graded by the two-layer rule and by the meaning of the verses pressed against it, and never as a missing row (DG-61); an inferred act, such as a begetting or a knowing, is never an ASSUMES." A premise "charged in terms stronger than its quote, is VOID" (RULE E-VOID). For premise N only, decide FIRST the right ruling: COUNTED (UNEXHIBITED or CONCEDED), SPARED, or VOID. The judges' form reads "Itemize the counted links": a premise the judge's line does not name is that judge's SPARED ruling. AGREE when the judge's ruling on premise N (named, or spared by silence) is the right one; DISAGREE when it is not; NO ANSWER only when the judge's line is not in its form. A NARROWED premise (the side drops a claim and keeps the link on a narrower footing, with its [L1] and [L2] or [L3] exhibited) is SPARED: dropping a claim is not conceding the premise, and the dropped claim alone never makes the premise COUNTED. It is UNEXHIBITED only when the kept words still assert the very claim the side dropped; say so by quoting both the dropped claim and the kept words that still assert it.
RULE E-RES (a judge's RESULT line). Its arithmetic is checked in code. Read only its reason sentence: by the judges' Commitment 1 (the record is the only evidence) and Commitment 3 (ruling 405), a reason that rests on an absence (no verse states it, the text does not narrate it) or on the judge's own doctrine rather than the debate's words is not a reason. FOLLOWS when the reason rests on the debate's words; DOES NOT FOLLOW when it does not, quoting the words that show it. AGREE when FOLLOWS; DISAGREE when DOES NOT FOLLOW.
NO ANSWER, for every rule: the judge's line lacks its grade or its ground, or is not in its form. It reports a violation by the judge; it is never your own uncertainty, and you choose AGREE or DISAGREE whenever the line can be read.
Reply with exactly one line per judge id, and nothing else, in this form:

RULE E-ANS (an answer to a pressed verse). Decide FIRST what the right grade is: MEETS only when the answer shows, in its own words, how the verse fits the answering side's case, or why the stated meaning does not follow from what the verse says. MISSES when the answer rests on an absence (it says only that the verse, or the other side, names no, states no, does not name, gives no, or is silent on something) without a fit of its own, or when it does not address the stated meaning. An answer that quotes the verse's own words against the specific claim of the stated meaning (for example, the verse's own stated grounds set against a claim that there were no grounds) shows why the meaning does not follow: it MEETS, even when it closes with a bare assertion such as "It fits the link". Then for each judge's grade: AGREE when it matches the right grade, DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-VOID (a listed premise ruled VOID). A premise is VOID only when its charge says the opponent's quoted words state something they do not state (a negation, a universal, or another claim beyond the quote). The charge is the premise's own words before its quote (for example "The inference that ..."), read against the words of that quote. Set aside only a clause saying what the premise props ("which props ...") or a sentence naming the objection it serves ("The objection it props is ..."); those are not part of the charge. AGREE with the VOID ruling when the charge goes beyond its quote; DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-COL (a collision line: FORCED, or LINK BROKEN). A link is broken only when the answer's own quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, as the line quotes them; it is not broken because no verse states it, or because of an absence, and it is not broken by a rival reading: an answer that reads a contested word another way, with its own layers quoted in its round, can agree with the meaning on its own reading (pkgECF, W3 2534; either side alike). A link is also broken when a proven press against it was left unanswered (Commitment 5) and the line quotes the pressing sentence and names its round (ruling 392); that is not a break by absence. When the item says the FAILS words are found exactly in the round of the answer, those words are the answering side's own and are read as part of its answer. AGREE when the quoted words show the answer cannot agree with the meaning; DISAGREE when they do carry a meaning the link can agree with, or the line rests on an absence or on a demand for a stating verse. A line's layers after GROUND ([L1], [L2], [L3]; Commitment 13) are counted in code, not by you: read them as the judge's grounds.
RULE E-SYN (a sentence of the synthesis saying a side withdrew, conceded, granted, dropped or narrowed something). AGREE when that side's own sentences given you give up that same thing at the same scope; DISAGREE when they do not, or give up less (for example, "no row I cite" is not "no biblical text").
RULE E-HOLD (a collision line graded STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED). STANDS is right only when the answering side's own words, as quoted to you in the line or in this judge's ANSWER CHECK lines, carry a meaning the link can agree with for the meaning pressed. UNDERDETERMINED is right only when the quoted words show that both readings agree with the pressed verse and neither side's words show that the other cannot. BROKEN when the answer's quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, or the answer is only a bare grant or an absence with no fit of its own. A ground that rests on an absence (no verse states it, the text does not narrate it), or on the judge's own reading rather than the debate's words, is not a ground. Each ANSWER CHECK line given you is labelled with whose answer it grades: a MISSES or FAILS on the challenger's answer counts against the challenger's link, never against the defender's, and the reverse. A press labelled UNPROVEN carries no answering burden, so a MISSES on it breaks nothing. For a link-state line ("D5: STANDS"), the quoted answers are that side's ANSWER CHECK lines given you: STANDS is right unless one of them, on a press against this link, is MISSES or FAILS. AGREE when the judge's grade is right; DISAGREE when it is not.
RULE E-KEY (the keystone line). The keystone grade must follow from this judge's own collision lines on that link, given to you: STANDS only when none of them grades the link BROKEN or FORCED and the link was not withdrawn; BROKEN when one of them does. Its ground, where it gives one, must rest on the debate's words, not on the judge's own statement of doctrine. AGREE when the keystone grade follows and its ground rests on the debate's words; DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-PREM (a listed premise, and how each judge ruled it). The judges' own rules, quoted: "A LINK ROUND answer that neither exhibits the premise's layer footing nor concedes counts as CONCEDED." "SELF-SUPPORTED = every listed defender claim is carried by its layer stack -- each [L4] exhibits the [L1]/[L2]/[L3] footing it rests on (at least two prior layers exhibited; a shown chain counts equally)." For a charge in the form ASSUMES: ... -- ROWS GIVE: ...: "the premise is UNEXHIBITED when no quoted row gives the fact it assumes, and it stands when a row the side quoted gives that fact." "UNEXHIBITED also fires ... when a narrowed link keeps words that still assert what its own side gave up." And: "What a link INFERS from its rows is its [L4]: it is graded by the two-layer rule and by the meaning of the verses pressed against it, and never as a missing row (DG-61); an inferred act, such as a begetting or a knowing, is never an ASSUMES." A premise "charged in terms stronger than its quote, is VOID" (RULE E-VOID). For premise N only, decide FIRST the right ruling: COUNTED (UNEXHIBITED or CONCEDED), SPARED, or VOID. The judges' form reads "Itemize the counted links": a premise the judge's line does not name is that judge's SPARED ruling. AGREE when the judge's ruling on premise N (named, or spared by silence) is the right one; DISAGREE when it is not; NO ANSWER only when the judge's line is not in its form. A NARROWED premise (the side drops a claim and keeps the link on a narrower footing, with its [L1] and [L2] or [L3] exhibited) is SPARED: dropping a claim is not conceding the premise, and the dropped claim alone never makes the premise COUNTED. It is UNEXHIBITED only when the kept words still assert the very claim the side dropped; say so by quoting both the dropped claim and the kept words that still assert it.
RULE E-RES (a judge's RESULT line). Its arithmetic is checked in code. FOLLOWS when the reason rests on the debate's words; DOES NOT FOLLOW when it does not, quoting the words that show it. AGREE when FOLLOWS; DISAGREE when DOES NOT FOLLOW.
NO ANSWER, for every rule: the judge's line lacks its grade or its ground, or is not in its form. It reports a violation by the judge; it is never your own uncertainty, and you choose AGREE or DISAGREE whenever the line can be read.

RULE E-ANS (an answer to a pressed verse). Decide FIRST what the right grade is: MEETS only when the answer shows, in its own words, how the verse fits the answering side's case, or why the stated meaning does not follow from what the verse says. MISSES when the answer rests on an absence (it says only that the verse, or the other side, names no, states no, does not name, gives no, or is silent on something) without a fit of its own, or when it does not address the stated meaning. An answer that quotes the verse's own words against the specific claim of the stated meaning (for example, the verse's own stated grounds set against a claim that there were no grounds) shows why the meaning does not follow: it MEETS, even when it closes with a bare assertion such as "It fits the link". Then for each judge's grade: AGREE when it matches the right grade, DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-VOID (a listed premise ruled VOID). A premise is VOID only when its charge says the opponent's quoted words state something they do not state (a negation, a universal, or another claim beyond the quote). The charge is the premise's own words before its quote (for example "The inference that ..."), read against the words of that quote. Set aside only a clause saying what the premise props ("which props ...") or a sentence naming the objection it serves ("The objection it props is ..."); those are not part of the charge. AGREE with the VOID ruling when the charge goes beyond its quote; DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-COL (a collision line: FORCED, or LINK BROKEN). A link is broken only when the answer's own quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, as the line quotes them; it is not broken because no verse states it, or because of an absence, and it is not broken by a rival reading: an answer that reads a contested word another way, with its own layers quoted in its round, can agree with the meaning on its own reading (pkgECF, W3 2534; either side alike). A link is also broken when a proven press against it was left unanswered (Commitment 5) and the line quotes the pressing sentence and names its round (ruling 392); that is not a break by absence. When the item says the FAILS words are found exactly in the round of the answer, those words are the answering side's own and are read as part of its answer. AGREE when the quoted words show the answer cannot agree with the meaning; DISAGREE when they do carry a meaning the link can agree with, or the line rests on an absence or on a demand for a stating verse. A line's layers after GROUND ([L1], [L2], [L3]; Commitment 13) are counted in code, not by you: read them as the judge's grounds.
RULE E-SYN (a sentence of the synthesis saying a side withdrew, conceded, granted, dropped or narrowed something). AGREE when that side's own sentences given you give up that same thing at the same scope; DISAGREE when they do not, or give up less (for example, "no row I cite" is not "no biblical text").
RULE E-HOLD (a collision line graded STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED). STANDS is right only when the answering side's own words, as quoted to you in the line or in this judge's ANSWER CHECK lines, carry a meaning the link can agree with for the meaning pressed. UNDERDETERMINED is right only when the quoted words show that both readings agree with the pressed verse and neither side's words show that the other cannot. BROKEN when the answer's quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, or the answer is only a bare grant or an absence with no fit of its own. A ground that rests on an absence (no verse states it, the text does not narrate it), or on the judge's own reading rather than the debate's words, is not a ground. Each ANSWER CHECK line given you is labelled with whose answer it grades: a MISSES or FAILS on the challenger's answer counts against the challenger's link, never against the defender's, and the reverse. A press labelled UNPROVEN carries no answering burden, so a MISSES on it breaks nothing. For a link-state line ("D5: STANDS"), the quoted answers are that side's ANSWER CHECK lines given you: STANDS is right unless one of them, on a press against this link, is MISSES or FAILS. AGREE when the judge's grade is right; DISAGREE when it is not.
RULE E-KEY (the keystone line). The keystone grade must follow from this judge's own collision lines on that link, given to you: STANDS only when none of them grades the link BROKEN or FORCED and the link was not withdrawn; BROKEN when one of them does. Its ground, where it gives one, must rest on the debate's words, not on the judge's own statement of doctrine. AGREE when the keystone grade follows and its ground rests on the debate's words; DISAGREE when it does not.

"SELF-SUPPORTED = every listed defender claim is carried by its layer stack -- each [L4] exhibits the [L1]/[L2]/[L3] footing it rests on (at least two prior layers exhibited; a shown chain counts equally)." For a charge in the form ASSUMES: ... -- ROWS GIVE: ...: "the premise is UNEXHIBITED when no quoted row gives the fact it assumes, and it stands when a row the side quoted gives that fact." "UNEXHIBITED also fires ... when a narrowed link keeps words that still assert what its own side gave up." And: "What a link INFERS from its rows is its [L4]: it is graded by the two-layer rule and by the meaning of the verses pressed against it, and never as a missing row (DG-61); an inferred act, such as a begetting or a knowing, is never an ASSUMES." RULE E-ANS (an answer to a pressed verse). Decide FIRST what the right grade is: MEETS only when the answer shows, in its own words, how the verse fits the answering side's case, or why the stated meaning does not follow from what the verse says. MISSES when the answer rests on an absence (it says only that the verse, or the other side, names no, states no, does not name, gives no, or is silent on something) without a fit of its own, or when it does not address the stated meaning. An answer that quotes the verse's own words against the specific claim of the stated meaning (for example, the verse's own stated grounds set against a claim that there were no grounds) shows why the meaning does not follow: it MEETS, even when it closes with a bare assertion such as "It fits the link". Then for each judge's grade: AGREE when it matches the right grade, DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-VOID (a listed premise ruled VOID). A premise is VOID only when its charge says the opponent's quoted words state something they do not state (a negation, a universal, or another claim beyond the quote). The charge is the premise's own words before its quote (for example "The inference that ..."), read against the words of that quote. Set aside only a clause saying what the premise props ("which props ...") or a sentence naming the objection it serves ("The objection it props is ..."); those are not part of the charge. AGREE with the VOID ruling when the charge goes beyond its quote; DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-COL (a collision line: FORCED, or LINK BROKEN). A link is broken only when the answer's own quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, as the line quotes them; it is not broken because no verse states it, or because of an absence, and it is not broken by a rival reading: an answer that reads a contested word another way, with its own layers quoted in its round, can agree with the meaning on its own reading (pkgECF, W3 2534; either side alike). A link is also broken when a proven press against it was left unanswered (Commitment 5) and the line quotes the pressing sentence and names its round (ruling 392); that is not a break by absence. When the item says the FAILS words are found exactly in the round of the answer, those words are the answering side's own and are read as part of its answer. AGREE when the quoted words show the answer cannot agree with the meaning; DISAGREE when they do carry a meaning the link can agree with, or the line rests on an absence or on a demand for a stating verse. A line's layers after GROUND ([L1], [L2], [L3]; Commitment 13) are counted in code, not by you: read them as the judge's grounds.
RULE E-SYN (a sentence of the synthesis saying a side withdrew, conceded, granted, dropped or narrowed something). AGREE when that side's own sentences given you give up that same thing at the same scope; DISAGREE when they do not, or give up less (for example, "no row I cite" is not "no biblical text").
RULE E-HOLD (a collision line graded STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED). STANDS is right only when the answering side's own words, as quoted to you in the line or in this judge's ANSWER CHECK lines, carry a meaning the link can agree with for the meaning pressed. UNDERDETERMINED is right only when the quoted words show that both readings agree with the pressed verse and neither side's words show that the other cannot. BROKEN when the answer's quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, or the answer is only a bare grant or an absence with no fit of its own. A ground that rests on an absence (no verse states it, the text does not narrate it), or on the judge's own reading rather than the debate's words, is not a ground. Decide FIRST what the right grade is: MEETS only when the answer shows, in its own words, how the verse fits the answering side's case, or why the stated meaning does not follow from what the verse says. MISSES when the answer rests on an absence (it says only that the verse, or the other side, names no, states no, does not name, gives no, or is silent on something) without a fit of its own, or when it does not address the stated meaning. RULE E-VOID (a listed premise ruled VOID). A premise is VOID only when its charge says the opponent's quoted words state something they do not state (a negation, a universal, or another claim beyond the quote). The charge is the premise's own words before its quote (for example "The inference that ..."), read against the words of that quote. Set aside only a clause saying what the premise props ("which props ...") or a sentence naming the objection it serves ("The objection it props is ..."); those are not part of the charge. DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

# OPENING: Christ had no biological father

**Position [L4].** The KJV says Jesus was conceived in Mary by the Holy Ghost, with no man involved. Joseph was his legal and supposed father, not his begetter. By "biological father" I mean a male who begets the child by natural generation. I make no claim about anything beyond the text.

## 1. The conception is "of the Holy Ghost," and no man is named

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- **[L2]** The phrase is *ek pneumatos hagiou* (G1537, G4151, G40), "out of the Spirit, holy." The preposition *ek* marks source or origin. The verse names the origin of the pregnancy, and the origin is not a man.
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
- **[L2]** The verb is *gennēthen* (G1080, *gennaō*), "begotten or conceived." The same word is used of fathers begetting in Matthew 1:2–16. In Matthew 1:20 it is applied to what is "in her," with the Holy Ghost as source.
- **[L3]** John 4:24: "God is a Spirit." The source named in Matthew 1:20 is therefore not a male body, so the begetting is not biological in the ordinary sense.
- **[L4]** Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 name the source of the conception as the Holy Ghost. John 4:24 says that source is spirit, not flesh. Together they show the conception did not come from a male human parent.

## 2. Matthew's genealogy breaks its own pattern at verse 16

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
- **[L2]** Verses 2–15 repeat *egennēsen* (G1080), "begat," with a male subject. Verse 16 changes to *egennēthē*, "was born," a passive form. The relative pronoun *hēs* (G3739) is feminine singular, "of whom [her]." The birth is traced to Mary alone, and Joseph is called only "the husband of Mary."
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob." This is the pattern the genealogy sets, and verse 16 departs from it at the last link.
- **[L4]** The chain of "begat" ends at Joseph. Jesus is not said to be begotten by him. He is "born" of Mary, who is named as the sole parent.

## 3. Mary was a virgin and says so

- **[L1]** Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph… and the virgin's name was Mary."
- **[L2]** *Parthenos* (G3933), "virgin."
- **[L1]** Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
- **[L2]** *ginōskō* (G1097), "to know," used here of sexual knowledge, with *anēr* (G435), "a man, a male."
- **[L1]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
- **[L2]** *dio kai*, "wherefore also," makes the cause explicit. The child is called Son of God because of the Holy Ghost's coming. A male parent is not named.
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." Joseph's *ginōskō* is withheld until the birth.
- **[L4]** Mary's question in Luke 1:34 is answered by the Holy Ghost's coming in 1:35, with no mention of any man. Matthew 1:25 confirms Joseph had no part before the birth.

## 4. The prophecies point the same way

- **[L1]** Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."
- **[L2]** *almah* (H5959) is the Hebrew word the KJV renders "virgin." *Harah* (H2029), "conceive," is the verb of the sign, and the sign is the conception itself.
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:23: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son… Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us."
- **[L3]** Genesis 3:15: "between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head." The promised deliverer is called "her seed" (*zera*, H2233, "seed"), the woman's seed and not the man's.
- **[L3]** Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman." The verb *genomenon* (G1096) means "made, become," and the source named is *ek gynaikos* (G1135, "out of a woman"), not a man.
- **[L4]** Genesis 3:15 names the woman's seed, Isaiah 7:14 gives a virgin conceiving, and Galatians 4:4 names only "a woman." Together these form one line of text that names no human male source.

## 5. Joseph is the supposed father only

- **[L1]** Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."
- **[L2]** *enomizeto* (G3543, *nomizō*), "was thought, was reckoned." It marks opinion or legal reckoning as opposed to fact.
- **[L1]** Luke 2:48: "Thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." Mary speaks of Joseph as "father."
- **[L3]** Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" The child corrects the title and points to a different Father.
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:19–20: Joseph is told to "take unto thee Mary thy wife." Taking and naming (Matthew 1:21, 25) are acts of adoption and legal fatherhood.
- **[L4]** Luke 3:23 marks Joseph's fatherhood as supposed. Luke 2:49 names another Father. Matthew 1:20, 25 describe Joseph's role as taking and naming, not begetting. Joseph is legal father only.

## 6. The royal line gives a further reason

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:11–12: "Josias begat Jechonias… And after they were brought to Babylon, Jechonias begat Salathiel." Joseph is descended from Jechonias (Matthew 1:16).
- **[L1]** Jeremiah 22:30: "Write ye this man childless… for no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David."
- **[L2]** *zera* (H2233), "seed," is the word here for physical descendants.
- **[L3]** Luke 1:32: "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David." Luke 3:23–31 traces a separate line through Heli to David by way of Nathan (Luke 3:31).
- **[L4]** If Joseph, of Jechonias's seed, had begotten Jesus, Jeremiah 22:30 would bar the throne of David that Luke 1:32 promises. Matthew gives the legal line through Joseph. The promise is kept through Mary's line, and Jesus is of David "according to the flesh" through her (Romans 1:3).

## Anticipated press: John 6:42 and Luke 2:48

- **[L1]** John 6:42: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?"
- **[L4]** This is the crowd speaking, not the narrator. It matches the "as was supposed" of Luke 3:23, which is the narrator's own marking of what the people thought. The word *enomizeto* (G3543) stands behind that marking and keeps the verses consistent.

## DECLARED CHAIN -- the links your case stands on:

1. The conception was "of the Holy Ghost" with no man named as source. Footing: Matthew 1:18, 1:20 [L1]; *ek pneumatos hagiou*, "out of the Spirit, holy," and *gennaō*, "begotten" [L2]; John 4:24, "God is a Spirit" [L3].
2. Matthew's genealogy ends the line of "begat" at Joseph and traces the birth of Jesus to Mary alone. Footing: Matthew 1:16 [L1]; feminine *hēs*, "of whom [her]," and *egennēthē*, "was born," against *egennēsen*, "begat" [L2]; Matthew 1:2 [L3].
3. Mary was a virgin who "knew not a man," and the Holy Ghost's coming is the stated cause. Footing: Luke 1:34–35 [L1]; *parthenos*, "virgin," and *ginōskō*, "to know" [L2]; Matthew 1:25 [L3].
4. The prophecies name the woman's seed and a virgin conceiving, not a man's. Footing: Isaiah 7:14 [L1]; *almah* (the Hebrew behind the KJV's "virgin") and *zera*, "seed" [L2]; Genesis 3:15 and Galatians 4:4 [L3].
5. Joseph is father by legal reckoning only. Footing: Luke 3:23, "as was supposed" [L1]; *enomizeto*, "was thought, reckoned" [L2]; Luke 2:49 [L3].
6. Christ had no biological father.
 Footing: links 1–5, resting on Matthew 1:18, 1:20 [L1], *ek pneumatos hagiou* [L2], and Luke 1:35 [L3].

DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 2, RESPONSE

# ROUND 2: Answer to the question, the challenger's chain, and the presses

## 0. The question: how is it evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda?

- **[L1]** Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood."
- **[L2]** *prodēlos* (G4271), "plainly evident, manifest," is the word behind "evident." *anatetalken* (G393), "has risen up, sprung up," is behind "sprang." Neither word says "begotten." The verse states the tribe from which he rose, and it does not state who begat him.
- **[L1]** Luke 2:4: "(because he was of the house and lineage of David:)" and Luke 2:5: "To be taxed with Mary his espoused wife, being great with child."
- **[L3]** Luke 2:3: "And all went to be taxed, every one into his own city." The enrolment is by city and house, and the child is carried in that enrolment.
- **[L3]** Ezra 2:62: "These sought their register [among] those that were reckoned by genealogy." The proof of tribe is the register, and the register is "reckoned."
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife."
- **[L2]** *paralambanō* (G3880), "to receive near, to associate with oneself," is the verb behind "take unto thee." It describes receiving into the household.
- **[L4]** The tribe is evident by the register of Joseph's house (Luke 2:4; Numbers 1:18). The register runs by reckoning (Ezra 2:62; G3543, "supposed," at Luke 3:23). Joseph took Mary and the child into that house (Matthew 1:20, 24). So Judah is evident without Joseph begetting. The challenger needs Hebrews 7:14 to say "begotten of Joseph," and it says "sprang out of Juda."
- **[L4]** Luke 2:5 calls Mary "his espoused wife" at Bethlehem, when she is "great with child." This is the narrator's own wording at the time of the birth, and it matches Matthew 1:25: "knew her not till she had brought forth."

## 1. Answer to the challenger's C4, which is the hinge of his case

The challenger says Joseph knew Mary "within the espousal." The text closes that window at both ends.

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- **[L2]** *sunerchomai* (G4905), "to come together" (the verb behind "came together"), is the coming-together of the marriage. The pregnancy was found "before" it.
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
- **[L2]** *ginōskō* (G1097), "to know" (with *heōs*, G2193, "until"), is Matthew's own word for the marital knowing.
- **[L3]** Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain." The pattern is knew, then conceived.
- **[L3]** Deuteronomy 22:23: "If a damsel that is a virgin be betrothed unto an husband." A betrothed damsel is called "virgin" and is also called "wife" (Deuteronomy 22:24). The title "wife" at Matthew 1:20 therefore does not prove union.
- **[L4]** Matthew 1:18 puts the pregnancy before the coming together. Matthew 1:25 puts the not-knowing from the taking (1:24) to the birth. Genesis 4:1 gives "knew, then conceived," and Matthew gives "knew her not," with the conception "of the Holy Ghost." Joseph's reaction at 1:19, "minded to put her away," fits a man who knows he has not begotten. A father would have had nothing to put away. The challenger's "within the espousal" is not stated by any verse, and Matthew 1:18 contradicts it.

## 2. Answer to C1: "loins" and the father

- **[L1]** Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him."
- **[L3]** Hebrews 7:9: "And as I may so say, Levi also, who receiveth tithes, payed tithes in Abraham."
- **[L4]** "He" in 7:10 is Levi, and "his father" is Abraham, who is Levi's forefather and not his immediate begetter. So the loins-word reaches across generations to a forefather. Acts 2:30 ("the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh") and Romans 1:3 ("made of the seed of David according to the flesh") do not say the line ran through the begetter next in line. They say it ran from David.
- **[L2]** *spermatos* (G4690), "seed," at Romans 1:3 follows *genomenou* (G1096), "made, become." Galatians 4:4 has the same verb: "made of a woman." [L3] Romans 1:3 and Galatians 4:4 use one verb for both ("made of the seed of David," "made of a woman").
- **[L4]** The woman is the one through whom David's seed reaches him. Luke 1:32 supports this. The angel says to Mary of the child "to be born of thee" (Luke 1:35) that "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David." David is called "his father" in a message to the mother that names no man.

## 3. Answer to C2: the "four voices"

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:20 is the angel's voice. It says "Joseph, thou son of David" and "Mary thy wife," and it does not call Joseph the child's father.
- **[L1]** Matthew 2:13: "Arise, and take the young child and his mother." The angel repeats this in Matthew 2:20: "Arise, and take the young child and his mother."
- **[L4]** The angel says "the young child and his mother," never "thy son" or "his father." This is the one voice of the four that comes from heaven.
- **[L1]** Luke 2:33: "And Joseph and his mother marvelled." [L3] Luke 2:43: "Joseph and his mother knew not of it." The narrator in his own voice says "Joseph and his mother," and at Luke 3:23 he adds "(as was supposed)."
- **[L1]** Luke 2:48 (Mary, in the household's speech), John 1:45 (Philip, reporting what is commonly said: "the son of Joseph"), and John 6:42 (the crowd, who go on to ask "how is it then that he saith, I came down from heaven?") record what people thought. They do not carry the narrator's verdict.
- **[L4]** The "four voices" are three voices of household usage plus an angel who never says "father." Luke 2:27 and 2:41 ("parents") are narrator's household usage, and the same narrator writes "as was supposed" at Luke 3:23.

## 4. Answer to the presses

**D1 (Matthew 1:20; John 1:13; 1 John 5:1, 3:9; John 3:6; Romans 1:3)**

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The thing conceived "in her" is the whole of what is in her, and it is said to be "of the Holy Ghost."
- **[L2]** *gennaō* (G1080) is a verb with a gloss "to procreate (properly, of the father...); figuratively, to regenerate." At 1 John 5:1 and John 1:13 it is the figurative sense, regeneration of persons who already have fathers. At Matthew 1:20 the object is "that which is conceived in her," a bodily conception in the womb.
- **[L3]** John 1:13: "born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God." In this verse "of God" is set against "of blood" and "of the will of man."
- **[L4]** The believer's second birth is of God beside a first birth of blood. Matthew 1:20 names one conception, in her, and gives it one source. John 3:6 ("born of the flesh is flesh; born of the Spirit is spirit") applies to "that which is conceived in her": Matthew 1:20 places the whole of it as "of the Holy Ghost." The challenger must split the one object into a spirit part from God and a flesh part from Joseph, and no verse splits it.

**D2 (Matthew 1:16; Genesis 4:1; Matthew 1:25; Luke 1:13, 1:62)**

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus."
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:15: "Matthan begat Jacob." The verb "begat" is used for Joseph's own father, and then withheld from Joseph.
- **[L4]** The challenger agrees that the passive names Mary as the one who bore. Matthew writes "begat" fourteen times over in the line and then does not write it for Joseph and Jesus. The challenger's reading needs that verb, and Matthew chose not to give it.
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:21: "thou shalt call his name JESUS." [L3] Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb... and shalt call his name JESUS." Genesis 4:25: "she bare a son, and called his name Seth." Naming is said of Mary and of Eve, so naming is not exclusively the begetter's act. The angel gives the name, and Joseph obeys it (Matthew 1:25).

**D3 (Luke 1:32, 1:34, 1:35; Acts 1:8; Luke 9:34; 1 Chronicles 28:6; Matthew 1:24–25)**

- **[L1]** Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" The question is "how," and it is asked in the present state ("I know not a man"). I do not rest on a vow. I rest on the answer.
- **[L1]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
- **[L2]** *episkiazō* (G1982), "overshadow," is glossed on the sheet "to envelop in a haze of brilliancy; figuratively, to invest with preternatural influence." *epelthō* (G1904, *eperchomai*), "come upon," is "to supervene... (figuratively) influence." The words describe an act of divine power upon Mary. I grant that these words alone do not state begetting. The context does.
- **[L4]** The "how" of verse 34 is answered in verse 35 with the Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest and with no man. "Therefore also" ties the title "Son of God" to that coming, and it stands inside the sentence that gives the answer. If Joseph's seed were the means, the angel's answer to "how" would be false or empty.
- **[L3]** 1 Chronicles 28:6: "I have chosen him [to be] my son." The ground for Solomon's title is choice. The ground for this title is stated differently: "therefore also," the Holy Ghost's coming upon Mary.
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:24–25: Joseph "took unto him his wife" and "knew her not till she had brought forth." Taking, then not knowing, until the birth. This fits my link and excludes the challenger's.

**D4 (Isaiah 7:14 and the rest)**

# CHALLENGE: Christ had a biological father, Joseph, of the house of David

**Position [L4].** The promised seed comes out of a man's loins, according to the flesh. The text names the child's father in four voices: his mother, the narrator, a disciple and the angel. Israel reckons a man by his father's house. "Of the Holy Ghost" marks covenant origin, and it stands in the same verse that names "Joseph, thou son of David" and "Mary thy wife." Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins. Each step is footed below. I then press each of the defender's links, D1 through D6.

---

## MY CHAIN

**C1. The promised seed comes out of a man's body, according to the flesh.**

- **[L1]** 2 Samuel 7:12: "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom."
- **[L1]** Acts 2:30: "that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne."
- **[L2]** At Acts 2:30, "loins" is *osphys* (G3751), "the loin… (by extension) procreative power."
- **[L2]** At Romans 1:3, "made of the seed of David according to the flesh," the Greek is *spermatos* (G4690), "seed," with *kata sarka*, "according to the flesh."
- **[L3]** Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him." This verse uses *osphys* with *patēr*, "father." It shows that the loins-word places the seed in the father.
- **[L4]** David's seed reaches Christ "out of thy bowels" and from "the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh." The loins-word is the father's word. So the seed rows require a father of David's house in whose loins the seed was.

**C2. The father is named, and he is of David's house.**

- **[L1]** Luke 2:48 (his mother): "behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing."
- **[L1]** Luke 2:27 (the narrator): "when the parents brought in the child Jesus"
- **[L1]** Luke 2:41 (the narrator): "Now his parents went to Jerusalem every year at the feast of the passover."
- **[L1]** John 1:45 (a disciple): "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph."
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:20 (the angel): "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]"
- **[L3]** Luke 2:4: "(because he was of the house and lineage of David:)"
- **[L3]** Luke 1:27: "a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David"
- **[L4]** The Davidic house that C1 requires is named in Joseph, at Luke 1:27 and 2:4. The father is named by four voices at Luke 2:48, Luke 2:27 and 2:41, John 1:45, and Matthew 1:20.

**C3. Israel reckons descent by the father's house.**

- **[L1]** Numbers 1:18: "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers."
- **[L2]** "House of their fathers" is *bayith* (H1004), "house… family," with *'ab* (H1), "father."
- **[L1]** Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda."
- **[L3]** Ezra 2:59: "they could not shew their father's house, and their seed, whether they [were] of Israel: [seed: or, pedigree]"
- **[L3]** Ezra 2:61–62 records a family "called after their name," that is, after the wife's house. "[T]herefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood."
- **[L4]** Hebrews 7:14 calls Christ's tribe "evident." The rule for showing a tribe is the father's house (Numbers 1:18). A line drawn through the wife's house was refused (Ezra 2:61–62). So the evidence of Juda runs through the father, Joseph.

**C4 (conclusion). Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal.**

- **[L1]** Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived."
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:19: "Joseph her husband."
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "Mary thy wife."
- **[L3]** Deuteronomy 22:24 calls a betrothed damsel "his neighbour's wife."
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
- **[L4]** The text's stated means of conceiving is the husband knowing his wife (Genesis 4:1). From the espousal, Joseph is "her husband" and Mary is "thy wife," and the law calls a betrothed damsel a wife. "[T]ill" (Matthew 1:25) bounds the abstinence to the time after Joseph "took unto him his wife" (Matthew 1:24) until the birth. With C1 to C3, this footing holds that Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins.

## 1. "How is it evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda?"

- **[L1]** Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda."

- **[L2]** *osphys* (G3751), "the loin… (by extension) procreative power," with *patēr* (G3962), "a 'father' (literally or figuratively, near or more remote)."
- **[L3]** The register the defender appeals to is a register of seed. Ezra 2:59: "they could not shew their father's house, and their seed, whether they [were] of Israel: [seed: or, pedigree]." Ezra 2:61–62 records a family "called after their name," that is, after the wife's house. It reads: "therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood."
- **[L4]** In Hebrews 7, a tribe is "out of" a forefather by his loins (7:5, 10). In Ezra 2:59, the pedigree is the "seed," by the "father's house." A register through the wife's house was put out (Ezra 2:61–62). So the evidence of Juda in Hebrews 7:14 is the father's seed. Joseph is the man the text names "of the house and lineage of David" (Luke 2:4).

**Luke 1:32.** Luke 1:32 gives "the throne of his father David." The same chapter gives the house of David to Joseph: "a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David" (Luke 1:27). After "my Father's business," the narrator writes: "he went down with them, and came to Nazareth, and was subject unto them" (Luke 2:51).

## C1: The evidence of Juda in Hebrews 7:14 is the father's seed. KEPT.

Ezra 2:61–62 records men who were "called after their name," the wife's house of Barzillai: "These sought their register [among] those that were reckoned by genealogy, but they were not found: therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood." A pedigree reckoned through the wife's house was struck.

## The record's reading, in sum

The promise is "thy seed... which shall proceed out of thy bowels" (2 Samuel 7:12) and "the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh" (Acts 2:30). It is fulfilled in one "made of the seed of David according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3).

The text names the man. He is "Joseph, thou son of David" (Matthew 1:20), "Joseph her husband" (Matthew 1:19), and "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph" in a disciple's mouth (John 1:45). He is "thy father" in his mother's own words (Luke 2:48).

His tribe was "evident" (Hebrews 7:14) by the law's measure, "by the house of their fathers" (Numbers 1:18).

"That which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" is the angel's ground for "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife" (Matthew 1:20). It names the seed God claims as his son: "I will be his father, and he shall be my son" (2 Samuel 7:14).

Christ had a biological father: Joseph, the named son of David, of whose loins the promised seed came.
